literal.prompt: Какой парк назван в честь древовидной юкки?

literalGroups.primaryGround: NPS directly states that the Joshua tree (Yucca brevifolia) is the namesake of Joshua Tree National Park (L25). The U.S. Forest Service confirms the species is in genus Yucca and has tree life form (L59-L64); all four choices are distinct national parks and only the Joshua Tree name matches this plant.
literalGroups.locator: NPS Joshua Trees L25-L26; USFS FEIS L56-L64

literalGroups.literal: Это Джошуа-Три. В его пределах встречаются две пустынные экосистемы.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NPS describes the Colorado Desert and Mojave Desert as the two named desert ecosystems, then separately describes a third high-elevation ecosystem in the Little San Bernardino Mountains with juniper and pinyon pine. “Two desert ecosystems” does not claim there are only two total ecosystems, so the wording is supported and retained.

literalGroups.literal: Зайон — парк Юты; в узкой части каньона стены достигают 1000 футов, а река Вирджин местами сужается до 20–30 футов.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The NPS page identifies The Narrows as Zion Canyon’s narrowest section, with walls 1000 feet tall and the Virgin River sometimes 20-30 feet wide; the page gives the Zion mailing address in Springdale, Utah.

literalGroups.literal: Грейт-Смоки-Маунтинс расположен на границе Теннесси и Северной Каролины; три главных входа в парк находятся в Гатлинберге, Таунсенде и Чероки.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NPS says the park straddles Tennessee and North Carolina and lists Gatlinburg, Townsend and Cherokee as the three main entrances.

literalGroups.literal: Акадия находится на побережье штата Мэн; парк защищает почти 64 мили побережья и включает более 20 гор.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NPS places Acadia on the Maine coast, reports nearly 64 miles of protected coastline and more than 20 mountains, and describes its forests and woodlands.

literalGroups.literal: Джошуа-Три — калифорнийский парк на стыке пустынь Мохаве и Колорадо.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NPS describes the Colorado and Mojave deserts and a third high-elevation ecosystem in the Little San Bernardino Mountains; the page also gives an address in Twentynine Palms, California.

absoluteDifficulty.audienceGround: For an adult beginner in a U.S. national-parks/general-nature quiz, this asks one direct namesake association among four well-known parks. It requires no botanical classification or multistep reasoning; the botanical description identifies the common tree rather than testing taxonomy.
absoluteDifficulty.judgment: This is an editorial judgment about an entry-level park/nature trivia audience. It is not a universal claim about every adult or every country; an independent reviewer may challenge whether familiarity with U.S. parks is broad enough for EASY.

supportingEvidence.support: NPS explicitly calls the Joshua tree the namesake of the park.

countClaimAssessment.literal: В его пределах встречаются две пустынные экосистемы.
countClaimAssessment.sourceStatement: NPS identifies a junction of three California ecosystems: Colorado Desert, Mojave Desert, and a third high-elevation ecosystem in the Little San Bernardino Mountains with juniper and pinyon pine.
countClaimAssessment.reason: The first two ecosystems are explicitly deserts. The text says there are two desert ecosystems, not two ecosystems total. NPS does not explicitly state that the third is a non-desert, so no stronger taxonomic claim is made.
